Phase 5.9 (s191) + Phase 5.9.5 (s192) + Phase 5.9.6 (s193) + Phase 5.9.7 (s194) + Phase 5.9.8 (s195) + Phase 5.9.9 (s196) + Phase 5.9.10 (s197) + Phase 5.9.11 (s198) + Phase 5.9.12 (s199) + Phase 5.9.13 (s200) + Phase 5.9.20 (s207, 2026-05-14, schema lift: int → int | list[int] for sum-of-blocks) - per-(champion, key) block_index_overrides for the ds.ability + ds.burst scorers. Default block_index=0 picks the first damage block of the canonical form, which matches the engine's pre-s191 `block_strategy="first"` behavior and is correct for ~95% of champions. A minority of champions have a later damage block that represents the realistic burst-window damage: the empowered/total/max variant that fires when canonical conditions are met (target poisoned, target chilled, full-charge windup, all bounces same target, sub-execute HP, full-channel duration, max sphere stacks, etc.). For ranking purposes (operator is comparing item builds for *their* champion in *their* combo), assuming amped conditions are met is the right model - same intuition as the engine already baking in `target_missing_hp_pct` and treating skillshots as landed. Keys are DDragon canonical ids; values map ability key (Q/W/E/R) OR repeat-variant token (Q2/W2/E2/R2 - Phase 5.9.5) to the 0-indexed block_index to use when the operator doesn't supply an explicit dict. Operator's per-call dict still wins per-key - registry fills any keys the caller didn't override.

Token-level lookup precedence (Phase 5.9.5): the burst combo walker checks the CANONICAL token first (e.g., "R2" for the Akali R recast), then falls back to the base ABILITY KEY (e.g., "R"). This lets a champion model its multi-step ability sequence with different block selections per token instance. `compute_ability_dps` is unaffected - it only iterates base spell keys (Q/W/E/R), so any R2-keyed entry is invisible to the mage scorer; token-variant entries only fire in the burst combo walker.
